ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The ULC is a non-reporting entity under the PCMLTFA for a stock photography merchant; no FINTRAC registration is required, and transaction-level AML obligations rest with payment service providers Stripe and PayPal. Institutional due diligence nevertheless mandates FATF-based PEP categorization and screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN/SSI list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under SEMA regulations. Enhanced due diligence is triggered only upon PEP or sanctions hits, adverse media, or high-risk jurisdiction exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be expressed in Latin alphabet characters; French is permitted; no transliteration doctrine applies in British Columbia. The name must consist of a distinctive element, an optional descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element for an unlimited liability company: 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'Unlimited', 'ULC', or 'U.L.C.' as prescribed by the Business Corporations Regulation. Alternative scripts may be used only as unregistered trade styles.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a Name Rejection Report in BC Corporate Online and may immediately re-file a revised Name Reservation Request. A written reconsideration may be submitted to the Corporate Registry (Name Approval, Ministry of Finance) with supporting evidence of distinctiveness, trademark registrations, or regulator consent letters. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, judicial review may be commenced in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. Sections 54 and 55 of the Business Corporations Act require a physical street address in British Columbia (not a post-office box) where service can be effected and a records office in British Columbia. A commercial virtual office with physical service acceptance satisfies the registry; for ULC treaty pass-through planning, real commercial substance (banking, records, director presence, income-producing activity) must be separately managed against domestic and cross-border anti-avoidance rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 5% probability within the first 24 months). The BC Corporate Registry performs no routine unannounced physical inspections for stock photography companies; Canada Revenue Agency audits are records-based and proceed by written demand.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, ss 10-12, 16, 27, 37; Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg 84/2002
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Incorporation Application submitted via Corporate Online; Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; unlimited liability shares may be issued without par value and for nominal or non-cash consideration, subject to the solvency test where shares are issued for property; no escrow account is mandated for cash subscriptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The first directors hereby approve the subscription agreement for one class of ordinary unlimited liability shares and any related shareholder subscriptions. (2) The registered office and records office of the Company shall be established at [Registered Office Address] in British Columbia, and the first directors are authorised to execute any lease or other document for such office. (3) The following persons are appointed as officers of the Company: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary. (4) All such officers and directors are authorised to file all statutory filings, open bank accounts, and carry out all matters required to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Reservation (or Numbered Company)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services - Corporate Online (online search) or Name Reservation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search through the BC Corporate Online registry; if a distinctive name is desired, file a Name Reservation and review the Name Report. Alternatively, use an incorporation number followed by 'B.C. Ltd.' as a numbered ULC. Retain the reservation number for filing the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed name or numbered company consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name reservation with a different distinctive word; if the name report raises trademark conflicts, obtain consent or choose another name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry through BC Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to BC Corporate Online, complete the Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles, and pay the filing fee. Attach the name reservation number or select a numbered company. Provide registered office address, records office address, director names, and incorporation date. The system issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Name Search Report or Reservation, if applicable
Names and consents of all first directors
Registered office address and records office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or returned, use Corporate Online to correct the Notice of Articles and refile; pay any additional fee if required; the registry may provide an expiry date for refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Officers and Adopt First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (company record, registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: In accordance with the First Board Resolution, the directors appoint the CEO, CFO, and Secretary, adopt the company's bylaws, authorize the issuance of unlimited liability shares, designate bank signatories, and set the fiscal year-end. Record minutes in the company minute book and file a copy at the records office.
required_dossiers: Written Minutes of the Inaugural Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any missing director or officer consent by having the individual execute a retroactive consent; if shares are issued for non-cash consideration, file a solvency certificate and any required contract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Create Statutory Minute Book and Register for Annual Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company registered office and BC Registry Services (annual report filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place all formation documents in the statutory minute book, including Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, bylaws, directors' register, share certificates, and share ledger. Set a corporate calendar for BC annual report filing and register for Corporate Online reminders. Maintain the registered and records office availability during business hours.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual report due date is missed, file a late annual report with the registry and pay the late fee; no administrative strike-off will occur before one year of delinquency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Business Licence and Ancillary Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City Business Licence Office, WorkSafeBC, and Local Fire Marshal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a commercial office or studio is used for the digital stock photo operation, apply for a business licence from the local municipality (e.g., Vancouver City Business Licence). Register and obtain occupational safety clearance from WorkSafeBC. Complete any fire safety inspection required for office occupancy. Since this is a non-industrial digital service, no industrial environmental permit is required.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of commercial address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal inspection identifies issues, remedy fire safety or occupancy deficiencies and reschedule inspection; if the licence is denied, request a variance or appeal to the municipal property use and zoning board.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based commercial photography / AI stock media activity, not a designated project under the Environmental Management Act; no EIA required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or VOC emissions; applicable only provincial waste management regulations, local stormwater and municipal solid waste limits for commercial offices, and WorkSafeBC occupational exposure limits for standard office equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under local fire code; commercial occupancy structural load inspection by the local building department if leasing a studio; WorkSafeBC registration and workplace safety clearance; emergency evacuation plan as per local code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency/Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC); portal: CRA My Business Account - https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html; BC provincial sales tax administered by BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch via eTaxBC - https://etax.gov.bc.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the BC ULC under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) via BC Registry Online and obtain the provincial incorporation number (no minimum capital). Step 2: Register the ULC with CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 to obtain the statutory 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts: corporate income tax (RC0001) and GST/HST (RT0001); a non-resident can register once it commences carrying on business in Canada. Step 3: Submit initial corporate intake/return and designating the registered office and Canadian-resident director required by the BCBCA. Step 4: If making taxable sales in BC, obtain a BC PST vendor account through eTaxBC (no monetary threshold). Step 5: If US-owned, file US Form 8832 (check-the-box) within 75 days of desired effective date so the ULC may be treated as a pass-through/disregarded entity for US federal tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Hybrid Entity Classification: Entity_Level_Taxation under the Income Tax Act (Canada) - a BC ULC is a corporation for Canadian tax purposes, subject to Part I federal and BC provincial corporate income tax on worldwide income; Pass_Through_Eligible under US check-the-box rules (Treas. Reg. 301.7701-3) for US federal purposes because shareholders bear unlimited liability; for GST/HST purposes, the ULC is a single registrant, and it may be eligible for territorial scope of taxation based on supplies made inside/outside Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box election exists; the ULC cannot elect to be a partnership/disregarded entity under the ITA. Available statutory elections and mechanisms: (i) US Form 8832 check-the-box election for pass-through status of a foreign eligible entity; (ii) ITA s. 216 election for non-resident owners of Canadian rental real estate (not the core business here); (iii) treaty-based residency tie-breaker under Canada-US Convention Art. IV(3) to establish place of effective management; (iv) hybrid mismatch/EIFA elections and funding structures under ITA ss. 18.4-18.6 to manage excessive interest and financing expenses; and (v) ETA registrations and input tax credit allocation elections for non-resident registrants. Election outcomes must be documented in the ULC's books to avoid GAAR recharacterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal Goods and Services Tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act) + BC PST (provincial sales tax under the Provincial Sales Tax Act, SBC 2012 c. 35); no HST in British Columbia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: C$30,000 - a registrant is required if worldwide taxable (non-zero-rated) supplies exceed C$30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the current and preceding three consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 240); non-resident digital suppliers of services/IPP to Canadian customers are subject to the same threshold and may use the simplified non-resident registration. BC PST: no monetary threshold - vendor registration is required from the first taxable sale/lease of goods or taxable services in BC, including online sales subject to PST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control mandate. Suppliers must issue an invoice (paper or electronic) no later than 15 days after the supply, containing the supplier's BN, recipient name, description and tax amounts (ETA s. 223). Electronic invoices are accepted, and GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) by registrants with annual taxable supplies over C$1.5M or when using a tax professional. Pan-Canadian e-invoicing interoperability via Peppol is voluntary. BC PST: vendors must keep sales records/invoices and file PST returns via eTaxBC; no government digital stamping or fiscal API clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: (a) Exported physical goods (prints or media): zero-rated under ETA s. 16 and Part V of Schedule VI when the supplier transfers possession/title to a non-resident and the goods are exported as part of a contract of carriage within the statutory time. (b) Licence of stock photos / generative AI visual assets: classified as a supply of intangible personal property (IPP) and zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V if the recipient is a non-resident not registered for GST/HST and the IPP is not for use/consumption in Canada; the contract must clearly convey a licence for use outside Canada. (c) Offshore services: a supply of services to a non-resident is zero-rated if rendered entirely outside Canada (ETA s. 9(b)); platform/hosting services must be verifiably performed outside Canada. The supplier must hold documentary evidence of non-resident status (foreign address, TIN), delivery/destination records, and repatriation of proceeds within the 180-day benchmark.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration or equivalent export reporting (Form B13A / electronic single-window filing) where physical goods are exported
Commercial invoice and licence/subscription agreement expressly stating the supply is made to a non-resident and the applicable zero-rating basis
Bill of Lading, airway bill or courier waybill evidencing exportation from Canada within the required period
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank advice confirming receipt of foreign proceeds in Canadian dollars within the 180-day repatriation deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA can reassess improperly zero-rated supplies within the normal 4-year period, extended to 8 years for misrepresentation attributable to negligence or fraud (ETA s. 298; ITA s. 152(4)). Overclaimed export refunds and input tax credits are clawed back with compound interest. Civil penalties: ETA s. 285 false-statement penalty of 25% of net tax understated or refund overstated (minimum C$250); ETA s. 280 failure-to-remit penalties. Criminal tax evasion (ETA s. 327 / ITA s. 239): fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment. CRA export audit practice requires contemporaneous export documentation (contracts, customs entries, carrier and bank remittance records) for digital supplies, and the application of general anti-avoidance rules (s. 245 ITA) may also unwind artificial export structures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (British Columbia Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the company's fiscal year-end; alternatively by the anniversary of the date of incorporation if the fiscal year-end has not been set
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 100 (approximately USD 74) per annual report; continued default leads to administrative dissolution after two consecutive years of delinquency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (if extra-provincially registered under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary date of incorporation or extra-provincial registration, due within 60 days after that anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 25 (approximately USD 18) for filings submitted after the 60-day grace period; revocation of registration and potential dissolution for continued non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Revenue Agency Corporate Income Tax Return (T2) and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the ULC's fiscal year-end for non-resident-owned or non-calendar corporations; standard T2 due date is 6 months after year-end with balance-due day 3 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty of 10%; daily interest compounding on unpaid balances

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return and Remittance (if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual filers; monthly/quarterly filers follow assigned periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty from 1% to 8% of net GST/HST payable depending on prior compliance; daily interest at prescribed rates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) Annual Return and Remittance (if taxable sales in British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Ministry of Finance (Consumer Taxation Branch)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the fiscal year-end for annual filers; installment filers have prescribed monthly/quarterly due dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% plus interest at 2% per month on unpaid PST; continued delinquency may lead to registration cancellation and collection enforcement

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for a BC ULC unless: (i) a shareholder holding at least 10% of issued voting shares makes a written demand; (ii) the corporation is a reporting issuer or publicly accountable enterprise; or (iii) a governing statute or regulator imposes an audit obligation. Exemption from shareholder-requested audit requires unanimous consent of shareholders for non-distributing corporations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) is required for publicly accountable enterprises (including reporting issuers); privately held ULCs may elect Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) as Canadian GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not require a separate annual UBO return for ordinary business corporations. However, the BC Business Corporations Act mandates annual confirmation of current directors and registered office information. The ULC must maintain an accurate central securities register reflecting all share transfers. If the ULC is a BC Land Owner, an annual transparent ownership declaration is due under the Land Owner Transparency Act. A 'transparency register' of individuals with significant control must be available for inspection upon regulatory demand, but no annual standalone filing is required except in land-holding scenarios.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of All Transfers of Shares
